cmes.note: Bright, fast, two-lobed CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and later in C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Its source is the large, fast prominence eruption seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304/284 after 2026-11-27T18:45Z in association with the C3.9-class flare from near to AR 14584 peaking at 2026-11-27T18:49Z, centered (~S07E69). It is also seen very faintly to the E in a bad (unusable) STEREO A EUV 304 imagery right after the data gap. The C3.9 flare is preceded by a C1.9 flare from the same Active Region (S12E72) peaking at 2026-11-27T18:19Z, which might be the explanation for the two distinct lobes of the same CME. The Active Region 14584 is located to the north of the large northern CH stretching along latitude S22, which might explain the northern deflection of the prominence and of the CME from the flare location.
